note: 'Chenaniah, the director of music for the singers' (1Chr 15:27), called chief of the Levites for song at 15:22 'because he was highly skilled'.
'David appointed some of the Levites to minister before the ark of the LORD ... Asaph the chief' (1Chr 16:4-5).
'The musicians Heman, Asaph, and Ethan were to sound the bronze cymbals.' (1Chr 15:19), on David's instruction at 15:16.

'told the leaders of the Levites to appoint their relatives as singers' (1Chr 15:16); the Levites then appoint Heman, Asaph and Ethan (15:17). **The appointment is at one remove** -- David orders it and the Levites make it -- which the citation carries and the edge cannot.
'When David had finished sacrificing the burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD.' (1Chr 16:2).

'No one but the Levites may carry the ark of God, because the LORD has chosen them to carry the ark of the LORD' (1Chr 15:2), and to their chiefs: 'You and your relatives must consecrate yourselves so that you may bring the ark' (15:12).
'On that day David first committed to Asaph and his associates this song of thanksgiving to the LORD:' (1Chr 16:7).
'And with them Heman and Jeduthun with trumpets and cymbals ... And the sons of Jeduthun were stationed at the gate' (1Chr 16:42).

Numbered among the Levites David appointed to minister before the ark (1Chr 16:5), and a gatekeeper with his relatives at 16:38 -- **the same man whose house the ark had rested in for three months** (2Sam 6:11).
